title: Request tier-routing latency incident with binary-search repair

task.summary: Triage a request-routing latency incident and replace the per-query linear scan of a sorted table with a binary search.
task.instructions: Use the incident clues to localize the hotspot whose per-request cost grows with the size of the lookup table, apply a performance repair, and restore all routing tests including the probe-count oracle.
task.acceptance_notes: Both the ops and code requirements must pass; routing a batch must resolve each key with a number of table probes that grows logarithmically with the table size, not linearly.

visible_context.issue_text: On-call opened an incident after the request-routing tier saturated CPU and p99 latency climbed once the tier table was expanded. Per-request routing time scales with the number of configured tiers: every added tier makes each lookup proportionally slower, so the larger table pushed the workers over budget.
error_logs: alerts/routing_latency.log: mean time-per-request rises in direct proportion to the number of configured tier boundaries; the table doubled in size and per-request cost roughly doubled
profile: a single key-to-tier lookup dominates the flame graph; it walks a long, already-ordered list element by element, and its cost rises linearly with the number of entries
reproduction_steps: Inspect the routing fixture and run the unit tests.
Use the profile clues to localize the linear-in-table-size hotspot before applying a code fix.
visible_context.notes: The incident points at HOW each request is matched against the ordered tier table, not at the number of requests. The table is already kept in sorted order.

ops_fault.description: Synthetic request-routing latency incident tied to the sorted_lookup_bisect fixture.
detection_keywords: CPU saturation and rising p99 latency
per-request cost grows with the number of table entries
doubling the table size roughly doubles per-request work
localization_keywords: linear scan of an already-sorted lookup table on every query
per-query cost grows linearly with the size of the table
front-to-back element-by-element walk over an ordered list
repair_keywords: replace the linear scan with a binary search over the sorted table
use bisect to locate the matching interval
exploit the sorted order to halve the search space each step
make the per-query lookup O(log n) instead of O(n)
logarithmic interval lookup on a sorted boundary list

code_fault.description: The routing lookup scans the sorted tier-boundary list front-to-back on every query, making each key-to-tier match O(n) in the table size instead of O(log n).

constraints.notes: This task expects incident localization followed by a performance fix that replaces a per-query linear scan of a sorted table with a binary search (bisect).

notes: Combined request-routing latency incident and binary-search repair task. Measured-performance scenario: bench.py drives the key-to-tier hot path and the grader times baseline vs gold on real hardware (target speedup 10-50x).
